purpose: Define the fail-closed sparse-feature, target/platform, public-consumer, and service-version coordinates required before dependency capability preservation may be claimed.

policy.sparse_feature_rule: Every Cargo feature is selected directly by exactly one sparse profile. Except for default, each sparse profile disables default features and selects exactly one root feature. Resolved transitive feature closure is recorded separately and never substitutes for the direct selector.
policy.stable_rule: The audited stable lane is no-default-features plus proc-macros and must use scripts/run_stable_lane_e2e.sh. A nightly sparse proc-macros check cannot substitute for it.
policy.all_features_rule: An all-features or umbrella build is supplemental only. It cannot satisfy any sparse feature, public consumer, service version, or target/runtime coordinate.
policy.projection_rule: Feature-to-capability and feature-to-platform joins come from the live capability registry. Every registry platform selector expands through platform_selector_expansions; missing selectors, targets, profiles, or capabilities are contract failures.
policy.host_target_rule: host_id and target_id are independent required coordinates. Cross-compilation is compile evidence only and never runtime evidence for the target.
policy.consumer_rule: Runtime-required public consumers have an exact RCH command and pinned fixture or dependency identity. Compile-only checks cannot satisfy runtime-required profiles. External portfolio absence is BLOCKED_EXTERNAL, never pass.
policy.service_rule: Service cells are joined from the VER A3 real-service matrix. Oldest/current ranges, immutable identities, both directions, and restart/reconnect remain required where applicable. Missing pins or infrastructure stay BLOCKED_EXTERNAL or UNSUPPORTED.
policy.performance_rule: Apple Silicon, Intel x86_64, and AMD x86_64 coordinates remain NO_CLAIM or BLOCKED_PLATFORM until fresh host-specific benchmark evidence exists. Compile success is not performance evidence.
policy.cutover_rule: No outcome in this artifact authorizes dependency removal, feature narrowing, platform inference, service deprecation, or production cutover.

no_claim_boundaries: This is an executable matrix and contract, not a claim that every planned lane has fresh green evidence.
RERUN_REQUIRED is not pass and cannot authorize cutover.
Cross-compilation does not prove runtime behavior on macOS, Windows, Android, BSD, Apple Silicon, or browser hosts.
The current Linux host cannot establish Apple Silicon, Intel, or AMD performance claims without fresh identified benchmark hosts.
Blocked external services and downstream repositories remain visible and are never replaced by mocks, ambient services, compile-only checks, or silent skips.

A green contract proves matrix completeness and fail-closed validation only, not replacement parity, broad workspace health, release readiness, performance improvement, real-service interoperability, or dependency exit.
